uncited: Constructs a 4x4 diagonal matrix that scales coordinates along the X, Y, and Z axes.
It solves the problem of applying non-uniform or uniform scaling transformations to 3D geometry within a homogeneous coordinate system.

It is distinguished from [Scaling and Rotation Matrix Construction](7986-scaling-and-rotation-matrix-construction.md) by excluding rotational degrees of freedom, and from [Transformation Matrix Construction](12879-transformation-matrix-construction.md) by excluding translation.

Indices `mat[i][j]` or `mat[i*4+j]` correspond to row `i`, column `j`.
Initialize `mat` as a 4x4 identity matrix or zero matrix, depending on implementation context.
The source implies setting specific diagonal elements.
Determine scale factors $s_x, s_y, s_z$ from input `s`.
The fourth row and column (homogeneous components) remain unchanged (typically identity values: `mat[3][3]=1`, others 0) unless explicitly modified by the caller.
- Precision issues may arise if scale factors are extremely large or small.
Originated in standard computer graphics literature for 3D transformations.
